properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/move_component.rs, 9 cases.

WHAT IT PINS: that a re-parent leaves ONE parent rather than two; that a Project containment is detached like any other, which is the cmp:identity case that motivated the operation; that an empty `detached` distinguishes "placed for the first time" from "moved"; that moving somewhere it already sits is idempotent rather than duplicating an edge; that self-containment and unknown endpoints are refused BEFORE anything is detached, so a refusal cannot half-apply; that a level relation which will trip hierarchy_issues is named at the moment of the move; and that a detachment always names the record_change preserving the previous parent.

THE REGRESSION CASE IS THE INTERESTING ONE. an_earlier_snapshot_does_not_silence_the_history_note pins a bug found by USING the operation on a real design rather than by reading it: the first implementation suppressed the history note whenever the child carried any snapshot at all. A snapshot from an earlier, unrelated epoch is no evidence that THIS move was recorded, so the rule went silent for precisely the long-lived node whose history is most worth keeping — wrong in the dangerous direction. Without that test the corrected condition would be one refactor away from being reverted as redundant.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: no test asserts that a bad level is REFUSED, because it is not — hierarchy_issues is the authority on decomposition defects and giving one rule two homes gives it two homes that can disagree. And nothing here checks what happens to the DEPENDS_ON, PROVIDES and CONSUMES edges of a moved component: they follow it unchanged, which means a move can put a contract across a wall it did not previously cross, and no check anywhere says so.
properties.findings:
RUN 2026-08-20: 9 passed, 0 failed. Whole crate 1110 passed / 0 failed across 106 binaries, which is exactly +8 tests and +1 binary against the 1102/105 baseline before this change — a foundation module was touched and nothing else moved.

ALSO EXERCISED AGAINST THE REAL DESIGN, not only fixtures: move_component was driven over stdio through the shared daemon against reflow2's own graph, on cmp:skills, which had carried two parents since before this session. Result: detached ["proj:reflow2"], already_there true, level_note null, history_note fired. hierarchy_issues went 3 findings to 2, and the multiple_parents finding is gone.

A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH KEEPING, because it looked like a bug in this work and was not: the first attempt drove a SECOND server process against the same store and got one tool, `reflow2_unavailable`. That is degraded.rs behaving correctly — the shared daemon holds the exclusive lock, so the second process degraded honestly instead of racing it. The "tool not found" error was truthful.
properties.name: A move leaves exactly one parent, and says what it detached
